description:
memory.rs:530-555 (default get_changes) and memory.rs:962-1000 (override get_metadata_changes) both walk relevant entries and accumulate created/updated/destroyed Ids with the same retain/contains dedup pattern. The only difference is the record_matches predicate gating each push in the override.

Impact: roughly 40 lines of duplicated logic. When the dedup rule changes (e.g. moving to the mail-server IdFate pattern per finding JMAP-826m.8), both copies need to be updated in sync. Tests don't catch divergence — there are no tests asserting that get_metadata_changes with all-None filters returns exactly the same arrays as get_changes.

Fix direction: extract a shared dedup walker taking a predicate closure. The default path passes |_| true; the override path passes its real record_matches. Tradeoff: closure-based abstraction is slightly less readable than two clear copies; if the dedup rule itself changes, only one place needs the update.
title: MemoryBackend.get_changes (default path) and get_metadata_changes (override) duplicate the same dedup walking logic, modulo the filter predicate — 40+ lines of near-identical code
